newsitem.title: USA: Enova seeks open Calif. electric mkt by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Enova seeks open Calif. electric mkt by 1998.

text.p: Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co has asked state regulators to allow all consumers to choose their electricity supplier starting in 1998, the utility said Tuesday.
SDG&E was joined in its filing by a coalition of the state's major industrial electricity users.
State legislation recently signed by Governor Pete Wilson calls for phasing-in deregulation of the electricity industry between 1998 and 2001.
The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) has proposed completing the transition to open access by 2003.

In a separate filing to the CPUC, the state's other two major investor-owned utilities, Southern California Edison Co and Pacific Gas and Electric Co, proposed a limited test of open access in 1998 and a tentative target for complete phase-in by the end of 2000.
But SDG&E said the only limitation on implementing direct access should be "the time necessary to install real-time meters so customers can compare usage on an hourly basis with ... prices."
The San Diego utility also said that traditional utility services like metering and billing should be unbundled as soon as possible so competitors can provide choice to consumers.
A final CPUC decision on the direct access schedule is not expected until late 1996 or early 1997.
